questions.def: Subordinate clauses need a subject and verb in the main clause.
questions.question: Although it was raining, ___ decided to go for a walk.

questions.def: "Because" introduces a clause that needs subject and verb.
questions.question: Because ___ late, I missed the beginning of the movie.

questions.def: "Despite" doesn't need "of". "In spite of" does.
questions.question: Despite of the rain, we still enjoyed the picnic.

questions.def: Past participle needed after "having" for a perfect construction.
questions.question: ___ him for years, I trust his judgment.

questions.def: Inversion is used after "so" + adjective at start of sentence.
questions.question: So tired ___ after the game, I went straight to bed.

questions.def: Inversion requires 'but' + subject + verb order.
questions.question: Not only is he intelligent, ___ also very kind.

questions.def: "Unless" already implies "if not".
questions.question: Unless if it rains, we will go to the beach.

questions.def: Perfect participle phrase shows completed prior action.
questions.question: ___ the report, she went home.

questions.def: Third conditional uses "would have" + past participle.
questions.question: Had I known, I ___ have acted differently.

questions.def: "Whether" requires a verb in present simple.
questions.question: Whether ___ or not, I'm going to the party.

questions.def: "The reason... was because" is redundant.
questions.question: The reason why he left was because he was bored.

questions.def: Implied conditional requires inversion with "had".
questions.question: ___ to the party, I would have gone.

questions.def: "Only then" requires inversion in the main clause.
questions.question: Only ___ did I realize my mistake.

questions.def: "Whereas" needs a contrast, using plural "others".
questions.question: Whereas some people enjoy city life, ___ prefer the countryside.

questions.def: Should be 'in spite of' or 'despite'.
questions.question: In spite the fact that it was raining, we went out.

questions.def: Perfect participle describes completed prior action.
questions.question: ___ the opportunity, she seized it immediately.

questions.def: "Such... that" requires inversion.
questions.question: Such ___ his enthusiasm that everyone joined in.

questions.def: "As long as" sets a condition in the present simple.
questions.question: As long as ___ hard, you will succeed.

questions.def: Due to + noun phrase; "because" or "as" + clause.
questions.question: Due to he was late, we started without him.

questions.def: Implied conditional requires 'had' + past participle.
questions.question: ___ the truth, I wouldn't have believed it.

questions.def: "No sooner... than" expresses immediate succession.
questions.question: No sooner had I arrived ___ the phone rang.

questions.def: "In order that" introduces a clause with subject + verb.
questions.question: In order that ___ pass the exam, you must study hard.

questions.def: "Scarcely" requires subject-verb inversion (had I).
questions.question: Scarcely I had entered the room when the lights went out.

questions.def: Reduced relative clause using the present participle.
questions.question: Not ___ the danger, I walked on.

questions.def: "Hardly" requires subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Hardly had ___ started speaking when he was interrupted.

questions.def: "Supposing" introduces a hypothetical situation.
questions.question: Supposing ___ win the lottery, what would you do?

questions.def: "Provided that" already indicates a condition.
questions.question: Provided that if you study hard, you will pass the exam.

questions.def: Implied conditional needs inversion: had + subject + past participle.
questions.question: ___, I would have taken a different path.

questions.def: "The moment" introduces a new clause requiring a subject.
questions.question: The moment ___ saw her, I knew she was the one.

questions.def: "Lest" implies 'in order that... not'.
questions.question: Lest ___ forget, remember to bring your passport.
